title: Sketch skin at the edges
summary: Zach's ruling made true: the hand-drawn look moves out of the core entirely and becomes a boundary transform. Byte-identical output, proven against the core's own live twin as oracle — and it fixes a 3.03× wobble distortion the core could not avoid.
changes: The ruling, verbatim. Zach, 2026-09-17: “I don't want the code base to be affected by the skin. Sketch skinning should be something very much done just like at the edges of the code base as a final rerender persay. nothing inside the code base should ever be driven [by it].” That is CLAUDE.md's own governing rule — the core is props in, DOM out — applied to a concern that had drifted inward. This lane decided where the transform belongs, proved it, and wrote the migration. It edited zero existing files under src/components/.

Correction first — it is 6 files, not 14. The brief said 14 components import the skin. Measured with grep -rl 'from "../skin' components/, it is 6. The other 9 contain the word “skin” only inside a comment pointing at where the token vocabulary is defined, and have zero module coupling. That difference is the whole shape of the migration.
VerdictnFiles
Guilty — real import of skin geometry6badge, block, port, portEdge, trace, traceTerminal
Innocent — comment mention only9blockMembers, button, dropdown-menu, editableText, foldingChevron, labeledPort, text, toggle, tooltip
Innocent — non-component2trace.routing.ts, tunnel.ts
The nine innocent files must not be touched. They read var(--bbox-skin-radius, var(--radius-lg)) inline — a value the edge supplied, resolved by CSS. That is how a skin is supposed to work. Rewriting them would be churn, and nine extra files in a merge with a concurrent lane for no behavioural gain.

The leak, measured on the live DOM. Not counted from source — read out of a rendered subtree that carries no data-bbox-skin attribute anywhere.
In an un-skinned subtree, the core still ships…measured
sketch path nodes10
bytes of sketched d string data5,124
sketch-outline SVG elements7
…of those, actually painted0
5,124 bytes of hand-drawn geometry computed and shipped into a board with no skin turned on, painting nothing. That is the ruling's own words made numeric, and it is the permanent-twin tax: trace.tsx:115-116 defines CRISP_STYLE/SKETCH_STYLE and emits both forms of every path forever so CSS can pick.

The decision: a boundary DOM pass. The core keeps emitting crisp geometry and its ordinary semantic data-slot attributes — nothing else. <SketchAtEdge> reads that subtree after layout and appends a drawn twin into the same parent, so it inherits the parent's viewBox and every enclosing transform — no host camera to replicate. Crisp suppression is pure CSS keyed on attributes the core already emits for its own reasons. React tolerates the appended nodes because React only reconciles nodes it created.

New files (all additive — the fenced directories were never touched):
apps/storybook-basics/src/skin/sketchAtEdge.ts — the pass; imports nothing from components/, and a test enforces that
apps/storybook-basics/src/skin/SketchAtEdge.tsx — the React shell, with its two honest limits stated in a LIMITS block
apps/storybook-basics/src/skin/sketchAtEdge.test.ts — 22 tests, including a drift guard that reads trace.tsx off disk
apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/SkinAtTheEdges.stories.tsx — 5 stories, every one carrying a real play-function proof
docs/peps/README.md + docs/peps/0001-sketch-skin-at-the-boundary.md — the decision-record convention, and the record
docs/SKIN-AT-THE-EDGES-MIGRATION.md — the per-file plan
findings:
PROOF 1 — byte-identical, against the core's own live twin as oracle.
The sketch generator seeds from the path string itself (seed: d), so the same d yields the same output wherever the call happens. That turns “does this match the look Zach approved?” from taste into string equality. The thing it is compared against is the shipped implementation, read live out of the same rendered subtree with the same props — nothing was re-derived.
measurementresult
paths compared6 of 6
all byte-identicaltrue
length of each sketched d656 chars (crisp input: 12)
M commands per sketched path2 — tldraw's two passes, intact
The crisp input M8 24L232 24 becomes 656 characters of two-pass hand-drawn geometry, and the core's version and the boundary's version agree character for character.

PROOF 2 — the boundary is strictly BETTER, and that was not expected.
sketchOutline.tsx exists in its current shape because the core may not self-measure (the rule that keeps it server-renderable). So it authors the path at a nominal size and stretches it with preserveAspectRatio="none". The components admit it: badge.tsx:102-107 draws every chip at a nominal 40×20, block.tsx:198-203 draws an auto-height Block at a nominal 200. A boundary pass runs after layout, where getBoundingClientRect() is ordinary.
Two chips, same rowreal pxviewBoxx-scaley-scale
narrow, in-core41.7 × 220 0 40 201.041.10
wide, in-core121.2 × 220 0 40 203.031.10
narrow, boundary41.7 × 220 0 41.66 221.001.00
wide, boundary121.2 × 220 0 121.2 221.001.00
The wide chip's “hand-drawn” wobble is stretched 2.75× more horizontally than vertically. Same defect on any auto-height Block: authored at a nominal 200 tall, rendered at 77 — wobble squashed to 38%. Moving this out of the core removes a compromise rather than trading correctness for purity.

PROOF 3 — the tunnel/sketch entanglement dissolves.
The lane's claim that triggered the ruling was that tunnel and sketch must coexist inside trace.tsx. They coexist in the DOM, but the pipeline is strictly sequential:

points → tunnelMouths(…) → drawnPath → sketchedTracePath(…) → sketched

Tunnel is semantic — "hidden" | "preview" | "revealed" | "off" decides which geometry paints. Sketch is cosmetic and consumes only the final string; sketchedTracePath is string → string and reads nothing else. So the boundary sketches whatever came out, knowing nothing about tunnelling. Verified on the tunnelled case: a tunnelled cable is two subpaths in one d, sketchPathData treats each M as its own run and pins that run's two endpoints — both mouths stay anchored with zero tunnel awareness. The entanglement was a DOM coincidence, not a coupling.

PROOF 4 — idempotent, measured from the pass's own returned stats.
Three consecutive passes over the same subtree, reported by the pass itself rather than inferred from node counts: {created: 3, reused: 0} → {created: 0, reused: 3} → {created: 0, reused: 3}. Zero redundant work, zero duplicated twins. A twin stores the exact source geometry it was built from as a DOM attribute, so validity is decidable from nothing but the document.

THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, rendered rather than argued.
An SVG feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filter is the most appealing answer on paper: genuinely a final re-render, zero JS, zero geometry knowledge anywhere. It is a different look wearing the same name, and it is in the gallery below so you can see that rather than take my word.
#DisqualifierHow it was checked
1No second pass. sketchPath.ts's own reading of tldraw 5.3.2 (module doc, point 3) is that drawing the outline twice is “doing most of the work, not the wobble”. A filter perturbs one rendered result.Countable: a drawn cable's d carries ≥2 M commands; a filtered path has exactly the 1 it started with. Asserted in the story.
2Endpoints move. sketchPathData pins the first and last point of every run so a trace cannot detach from its port dots — its own header calls a wandering endpoint “a correctness bug wearing a style's clothes”.A filter displaces every pixel, ends included, with no exemption. The pinning is unit-tested on all 5 path shapes.
3It catches everything. A filter applies to its whole subtree — labels and badge text included.Visible in the capture: the label under the filtered column is displaced too.
Also rejected: one injected primitive (core renders through a swappable <Path>) — it relocates the violation, leaving a skin-shaped hole in every component and losing the measurement win entirely, since a primitive rendered from inside the core still cannot measure itself. And keep the twins, compute at the boundary — half a step that keeps the 10-node/5,124-byte tax and still needs the core to know it might be hidden.

WHAT LOOKING AT THE CAPTURES CAUGHT — three defects the passing tests did not.
All 48 story files were green before any of these were found. Each was caught by opening the PNG and comparing columns, which is the argument for captures being evidence rather than decoration.
#DefectRoot causeNow guarded by
1Column 3 rendered with the default card fill and sans font, so it compared two different thingsMy story was wrong, not the design. I had left the skin attribute off the boundary column, but docs/peps/0001 explicitly keeps the token layer — only geometry moves. The capture caught the story contradicting its own record.Restructured into 4 columns: 3 is the production config (tokens + boundary), 4 isolates the independence claim
2Badge outlines collapsed to a stray 12×12 markA real hazard class of the approach: a boundary-injected node lives in the host's cascade, and Badge carries shadcn's [&>svg]:size-3 (there so an icon inside a chip is 12px), which beats an SVG's width/height attributes. Declared 121.2×22, rendered 12×12.Size written as inline style, plus a play-function assertion on the twin's own getBoundingClientRect — attributes alone asserted green straight through this
3Port dots read as a bullseye — a second ring inside the coloured oneA dot's state rings are box-shadow layers outside the element, so getBoundingClientRect returns the 12px dot while the ring the eye reads is larger. Drawing on the element box put the line in the wrong place.Solved, not deferred. The two numbers the core uses privately are already in the computed box-shadow as its spread radii, and the algebra reduces exactly: SURFACE*2 + STATE*3 == 3*s2 - s1. The edge now emits viewBox 0 0 25 25 and pen 3 — identical to the core's, asserted per state
Defect 3 was listed as the migration's one open geometry question in my first draft. It is now closed, with one honest caveat: the box-shadow parser is DOM archaeology that exists only so this PoC could show correct geometry without editing a fenced component. At migration port.tsx publishes those numbers the same way M6 publishes its colour and the parser is deleted — the code says so at the seam.

THE LIMIT YOU ASKED ME TO NAME.
Two classes of chrome a “final rerender at the edges” cannot fully cover. Both follow from one fact — a pass that runs after the frame cannot be inside it — so neither is fixable by a better implementation. They are the price of the ruling, not of the code.
ClassWhat happensMitigation
In-flight geometry (live drag, animated route)The drawn twin trails the crisp geometry by up to one frame (~16ms): crisp updates in React's commit, the twin in the effect after it. The in-core design had no gap — it computed the sketch during the same render.Show crisp while a gesture is live, redraw on gesture end. That is what tldraw itself does, and it is cheaper than sketching 60 paths a second.
First paint under SSRThe pass cannot run on the server or before hydration, so server-rendered HTML paints crisp for one frame, then swaps. The in-core design shipped the twin in the SSR output and was correct in the first painted frame.None that keeps the ruling. A FOUC-class artifact: invisible in Storybook, real in apps/docs.
Neither affects a static canvas, which is how these components are looked at essentially all of the time. A third, smaller cost: semantic seeds (badge:${size}:${shape}) are props the edge cannot see, so they need one data-bbox-seed attribute to travel — migration item M7.

THE TRAP A BUILD LANE WOULD FALL INTO — and the barrier that prevents it.
The skin hides a crisp border by making it transparent while keeping its 2px width, so nothing moves (skin.test.ts pins that width across every skin). Measured on styles--sketch: a Block's computed border-color under the sketch skin is rgba(0, 0, 0, 0).

So a boundary pass that does the obvious thing — getComputedStyle(el).borderColor — gets transparent and draws invisible outlines, while still passing every test that only checks an element exists. The element's resolved colour is exactly the one thing the skin has already destroyed by the time the edge looks at it.

Fix, verified live: where a state owns the colour, the component publishes it in a channel the skin never writes — one added custom property. Confirmed working: a port dot published oklch(0.65 0.19 48) and an injected child <path> with stroke: var(--bbox-ink-state, …) resolved exactly that. This is not a skin import — the component names a colour it already computed, which is strictly more honest than today, where the same colour is passed as a React prop into a skin component. This is migration item M6, a barrier: land it first, alone.

THE MIGRATION — docs/SKIN-AT-THE-EDGES-MIGRATION.md.
Per-file, with line numbers against base 064be4b. M6 is a barrier (above) — land alone; then M1–M5 run in parallel on disjoint files; M7–M8 are cleanup.

The one-command acceptance test for the whole exercise: grep -rl 'from "../skin' apps/storybook-basics/src/components/ returns nothing.

One warning for whoever runs it: BoundaryMatchesCoreExactly's oracle is the core's twin. Capture the golden strings before deleting the core's half, or the byte-identity evidence dies with it.

Provenance. No math was re-derived — every generator is imported from sketchPath.ts, which carries a thorough in-file citation (tldraw 5.3.2 PathBuilder.mjs's toDrawD, GeoShapeBody.mjs, @tldraw/utils's rng ported verbatim). The DOM-walk and twin protocol are ours, ad hoc, and say so. The architectural model is cited: SystemSketch already does exactly this — it has zero custom sketch geometry, no roughjs, no feTurbulence, and delegates the hand-drawn look to tldraw's own dash: "draw" shape prop at the host boundary (/home/bam/systemsketch/src/inspector/inspectorModel.ts:742, read read-only). Zach's ruling is asking bbox-ui to adopt the split his other project already uses.

Correction to the brief: it said docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md “classifies sketchPath.ts already”. It does not — zero matches for sketch, skin, wobble or jitter. That file scopes itself to src/components, so all of src/skin/ is uncovered. The rows to add are drafted at the end of the migration doc; I did not edit that file, since its scope line is a decision rather than an oversight.

Gates — all three green, none lower. typecheck clean · pnpm test-stories 47 files / 192 tests → 48 / 197 · vitest --project=unit 24 / 393 → 25 / 415. Every visual claim above is measured (getBoundingClientRect, getComputedStyle, real d strings read out of the DOM); storyRenders[0].reportedException was never consulted. Write-set boundary respected absolutely: git status shows zero modifications to any existing file under src/components/ or src/hosts/ — this lane is additive only.

Not done, deliberately. The migration itself — a concurrent lane owns all 14 files under components/. The port.tsx ring-offset question in M4 is flagged rather than guessed. The PoC covers the three shape classes all six guilty files reduce to (arbitrary path, rounded rect, ellipse) via block/badge/port-dot/trace-line; adding portEdge's group box and traceTerminal's ring is a one-line selector change each, with no new mechanism — which is what makes the migration mechanical rather than exploratory.

stories.title: Side by side — the whole argument in one frame
stories.look_for: Four columns. 1 is the crisp core, no skin anywhere. 2 is today's mechanism (the core computing its own sketch). 3 is the real production configuration — the skin ATTRIBUTE still supplies tokens (no fill, informal font, 2px stroke), but no component computes a wobble; every drawn line comes from the boundary. Compare 2 and 3 across traces, blocks, chips and port rings: that is the look, unchanged. 4 drops the skin attribute entirely — the core does not know a skin exists and is simply drawn over. ONE known gap, visible on the dots: the drawn ring's SHAPE now matches the core exactly (viewBox and pen width asserted equal, per state), but its COLOUR falls back to the skin's ink instead of the state's orange/green, because publishing that colour needs a one-line component edit this lane was fenced out of. That is migration item M6, and it is why M6 is a barrier.

stories.title: Byte-identity — crisp, core twin and boundary twin all visible
stories.look_for: Nothing is hidden here, so all three layers paint at once: the crisp path, the core's own drawn twin, and the boundary's. They overlap exactly. The play function asserts the two sketched d strings are equal character for character — 6 of 6, 656 chars each — including the tunnelled case on the right, where a cable is two subpaths in one d.

stories.title: Measured, not nominal — what the boundary fixes
stories.look_for: Look at the two chips at the bottom. On the LEFT (in-core) both outlines are authored at a 40-unit viewBox and stretched to fit — 1.04x for the narrow chip, 3.03x for the wide one, against 1.10x vertically either way. You can see the result: the wide chip's outline overshoots its ends and the narrow one has a stray mark. On the RIGHT the boundary measured each element and drew at 1.00/1.00. Note the right column deliberately keeps the default card fill and divider — this story isolates GEOMETRY, so the skin's token layer is off; the side-by-side capture above shows the full production look.

stories.title: Rejected — the feTurbulence filter, rendered not argued
stories.look_for: Left is the chosen geometric transform; right is an feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filter, the option that looked best on paper. The right side is wavy rather than drawn — no second pen pass, and it has no concept of pinning a trace to its endpoints. Note the label under it is displaced too: a filter catches its whole subtree, text included.

stories.title: Idempotent — three passes, reported by the pass itself
stories.look_for: The pass-log line is the pass's own returned stats, not an inference from node counts: created 3, then reused 3, reused 3. Press the button to re-run. A twin records the exact geometry it was built from, so validity is decidable from the document alone.

stories.title: Styles · Side By Side — the review surface, still intact
stories.look_for: Your existing skin gallery, untouched and still green. The toolbar skin picker still switches all three skins live. A correct architecture that loses this surface would be a failed deliverable, so it is in the report as evidence rather than a claim.
